sources.entry: Finding a problem at the bottom of the Google stack

summary.name: SRE keeps digging to prevent problems
summary.one_liner: A Google Cloud blog post walking through a real SRE incident in which GFE machine errors were traced down to failed rack casters causing CPU throttling.
use_cases: Learning how SREs trace a production incident down to hardware
Understanding incident mitigation by draining traffic before root cause
Studying cross-team incident investigation between SRE and hardware ops
Preparing an example for an SRE training or talk
Seeing how to file a hardware repair bug with clear symptoms
summary.what_it_does: The post describes a real Google incident in which GFE (Google front end) machines in the edge network produced abnormal errors. The on-call SRE drained the affected machines to stop customer impact, then found packet loss isolated to one rack and correlated BGP flapping. Kernel logs showed CPU throttling from package temperature thresholds, and a monitored CPU spike in the BGP process matched the errors. Neighboring racks were unaffected. The hardware team found that failed rack casters let the loaded rack tilt, disrupting liquid coolant flow. The post then covers the caster repair and the systematic replacement of other racks with the same issue.
notable: Traces a software symptom (GFE errors, BGP flapping) down to a physical cause (failed rack casters)
Shows drain-first mitigation followed by root-cause investigation
Describes how a hardware bug ticket was written with clear symptoms and actions taken
caveats: This is a narrative blog post, not a software tool or product, so there is nothing to install or use
Describes internal Google infrastructure practices; specifics may not apply directly to other environments
